items.title: Live: Headline inflation eases more than expected but RBA rate hike risk remains
items.description: Headline inflation has eased to an annual rate of 4 per cent in May, down from 4.2 per cent in April, according to the latest ABS data. Follow live.

items.title: Angus Taylor says he believes in 'a version' of multiculturalism
items.description: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor will not break a decades-long bipartisan position of supporting multiculturalism, saying he still supports "a version" of it after dithering under questioning yesterday.

items.title: Live: Pauline Hanson says Socceroos represent her vision of monoculture
items.description: Hanson says she is "delighted" monoculturalism is being debated and says the Australian soccer team represents her vision for a national "monoculture". Follow live.

items.title: Police to review case of Epstein accuser Virginia Giuffre
items.description: The interactions Jeffery Epstein accuser Virginia Giuffre had with Australian police before her death will be reviewed, WA's police commissioner confirms.

items.title: Karl Stefanovic's interview with Tommy Robinson taken offline
items.description: Today show host-turned-podcaster Karl Stefanovic has had his interview with far-right extremist Tommy Robinson taken down from social media and podcast platforms.

items.title: 'I love you': Sydney shark attack survivor's first words to family
items.description: A Sydney mother mauled by a shark at Coogee Beach almost a fortnight ago has spoken her first words after briefly waking from an induced coma.

items.title: Bird flu prompts Papua New Guinea to ban Australian chicken and egg imports
items.description: Australia's largest chicken meat buyer, Papua New Guinea, suspends Australian poultry and egg imports due to the H5N1 bird flu outbreak, even though Australian authorities say there is no evidence the virus has spread.

items.title: Self-managed super sector blindsided by Labor–Greens deal on tax package
items.description: A ban on self-managed super funds borrowing money to buy housing has blindsided the sector, which says Labor should instead target "unscrupulous" operators spruiking property as an investment.

items.title: 'Doesn't seem right': Why Socceroos won't play for a draw against Paraguay
items.description: A draw would be enough for the Socceroos to progress from their World Cup group, but according to defender Jason Geria, playing for anything less than a win does not sit right with this group.

items.title: Qantas A380 to be inspected urgently after cracks found
items.description: Airbus says it will inspect 16 A380 planes, including one Qantas plane, after cracks were found in a key wing component.

items.title: 'Historic blunder': US Senate votes to seek to prevent further military action in Iran
items.description: It is the 10th time the Senate has tried to stop the war, and the outcome, on a vote of 50–48, is a stunning turnaround from past efforts.

items.title: DRC Ebola outbreak grows to become one of worst recorded
items.description: There are now more than 1,000 confirmed cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and 267 people have died, local officials say.

items.title: Bondi terror attack hero pleads not guilty to alleged assault on father
items.description: Ahmed Al Ahmed has pleaded not guilty to allegations he assaulted and intimidated his father during an incident in March.

items.title: Matt Wright sued for negligence after airboat allegedly crashed into tree
items.description: A man who says he suffered a "psychiatric injury" after witnessing injuries sustained by his wife in a 2023 airboat crash is suing tour operator and Netflix star Matt Wright for negligence.

items.title: Heartbroken Daryl Braithwaite will miss everything about performing
items.description: The Aria Hall of Fame inductee speaks emotionally to the ABC about his decision to give up live performances, saying it has broken his heart to see how appreciative people have been.

items.title: Farming couple who met at bus stop celebrate 70 years of love on the land
items.description: Farming couple Bill and Val Collins share their secrets to a long marriage as they celebrate their platinum wedding anniversary.

items.title: When Siri Hustvedt felt her husband's ghost, she turned to science
items.description: The author of What I Loved has published a moving memoir drawing on letters and journals documenting the last days of Paul Auster, her partner in life and writing.

items.title: Illegal e-bikes crushed after Tweed-Byron police crackdown
items.description: Police on the NSW Far North Coast have confiscated and crushed 35 e-bikes, and warn even more could soon be trashed as the crackdown continues.

items.title: Family left 'shattered', 'traumatised' by woman's murder, court told
items.description: Jessie James Tumaliuan has been sentenced to more than two decades in jail for the violent murder of his estranged wife in March last year.

items.title: 'Significant errors' in 'preventable' death of baby in murder-suicide
items.description: A coroner finds the "upsetting" death of a nine-month-old baby in the Barossa Valley in a public murder-suicide by her "manipulative, self-absorbed and dangerous" father could have been prevented.

items.title: Women charged after allegedly trafficking cocaine, meth on Spirit of Tasmania
items.description: Two women are alleged to have had traffickable quantities of meth and cocaine in their car when they evaded police upon exiting the Spirit of Tasmania ferry in Devonport.

items.title: Coroner warns of dangers of power boards after fatal house fire
items.description: A Victorian coroner has issued a warning over the safety of power boards following a house fire that claimed the life of a 77-year-old man.

items.title: Why your power bill may rise despite the lower default market offer
items.description: Some electricity users have been hit with higher charges, despite all the talk of the lower default market offers. Retailers say a rebalancing of supply and usage charges is the cause, but there are signs some are clawing back profit by raising their cheapest plans.

items.title: Australians financially supporting family in Lebanon say they have no other option
items.description: Lebanese Australians, who have spent thousands of dollars to help their loved ones survive a two-and-a-half-year war, bear a financial burden that also comes with an emotional toll.

items.title: UN inquiry accuses Israel of deliberately targeting and killing Palestinian children
items.description: The Israeli government is condemning the inquiry and rejecting its findings, labelling the United Nations report "deeply flawed" and full of "errors and distortions" designed to push a "politically driven anti-Israel narrative".
